name: Initial high-flow nasal cannula flow escalation
explanation: Increasing flow and FiO2 to meet high inspiratory demand is reasonable initial management while closely monitoring for respiratory fatigue.
source: Roca O, et al. J Crit Care 2016;35:200-5; teaching-convention

name: Timely invasive mechanical ventilation
explanation: Proceeding with prompt endotracheal intubation when work of breathing remains high and oxygenation fails avoids emergency crash intubation.
source: Kang BJ, et al. Intensive Care Med 2015;41:623-32; Roca O, et al. 2016

name: Delayed intubation in progressive respiratory failure
explanation: Intubation was delayed despite sustained tachypnoea, worsening hypoxaemia, and severe patient work of breathing.
source: Kang BJ, et al. Failure of high-flow nasal cannula therapy may delay needed intubation and increase mortality. Intensive Care Med 2015;41:623-32

name: Post-intubation lung-protective ventilation
explanation: Setting initial tidal volumes matched to predicted body weight (<= 6-7 mL/kg PBW) immediately upon intubation protects against ventilator-induced lung injury.
source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023

name: Unadjusted default ventilator volume after intubation
explanation: Leaving an adult patient on default uncalibrated ventilator settings (e.g. 450-500 mL in a small female with PBW < 55 kg) delivers excessive tidal volumes.
source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8

name: Diuretic therapy in acute sepsis with hypovolaemia
explanation: Administering loop diuretics for severe pneumonia without cardiogenic fluid overload risks hypoperfusion and worsening acute kidney injury.
